title: PRISM-Physics: Causal DAG-Based Process Evaluation for Physics Reasoning
notes: physics_science: must-cite - step-level physics evaluation: reference solutions become DAGs of formulas scored by ancestor-closure credit with rule-based symbolic formula matching, validated against expert scores (Kendall tau-b 0.346, against 0.294 for an LLM judge and 0.213 for PhysReason's PSAS-S), so the May claim that physics benchmarks only match outcomes no longer holds.

title: HiPhO: How Far Are (M)LLMs from Humans in the Latest High School Physics Olympiad Benchmark?
notes: physics_science: must-cite - 13 physics olympiad exams from 2024-2025 (360 problems, 519 subquestions) graded at answer and step level by applying the official marking schemes with an LLM judge checked against human graders; a recent, step-scored physics benchmark at a top venue.

title: SymPyBench: A Dynamic Benchmark for Scientific Reasoning with Executable Python Code
notes: physics_science: must-cite - closest prior art to EngTrace's generator: 15,045 university-physics problems, each parameterised as executable Python that recomputes the answer for any input, with step-by-step solutions, partial credit over subproblems and consistency metrics across variants; the revision must say exactly how EngTrace differs (engineering contexts, milestone checks inside free-form traces, expert-validated step evaluation).

title: Sci-Rho: A Multilingual Visually-Grounded Symbolic Benchmark for STEM Problems
notes: physics_science: must-cite - expert-written Python templates (606 per language in seven languages; physics is one of five GCSE/A-level subjects) generate each instance together with a gold step-by-step solution, scored by worst-case accuracy over variants and an LLM-judged step-level F1; it already pairs generated instances with gold steps, so EngTrace must not claim to be alone in doing so (it differs in engineering scope, text-only items and deterministic milestone checks).

title: SciDA: Scientific Dynamic Assessor of LLMs
notes: physics_science: must-cite - over 1,000 olympiad-level numerical problems in mathematics, physics, chemistry and biology whose parameters are re-sampled every evaluation round; accuracy falls 10-20 points under randomisation, direct evidence for EngTrace's generated-instance design, though only final answers are scored.

title: AtmosSci-Bench: Evaluating the Recent Advance of Large Language Model for Atmospheric Science
notes: physics_science: must-cite - a physical-science benchmark built much like EngTrace: 67 expert-written templates with LLM-drafted, expert-verified Python solvers instantiated 10 or 30 times, plus 391 open-ended questions scored by a numeric-tolerance, SymPy and LLM-judge cascade, but scored on final answers only; template generation with code-computed answers is therefore not new to physical domains.

title: How Good Are Frontier Models at Physics? Expert Re-Grading Reveals Broken Evaluations and Near-Saturation of Leading Benchmarks
notes: physics_science: must-cite - physicists audited answers marked wrong on six physics benchmarks (including the cited UGPhysics and PHYBench) and found reference-solution and grader defects behind almost all of them (12 genuine model errors in 250 pooled rejections); strong support for code-derived gold and expert-validated checks, and a warning against quoting physics benchmark scores at face value.

title: Right Answer, Wrong Method: Shortcut Hacking Misleads the Evaluation of LLM Reasoning on Frontier Science Benchmarks
notes: physics_science: must-cite - PhD experts labelled 300 solutions and an LLM panel scaled the audit: 8.2%-44.1% of answers credited as correct on science benchmarks (SciBench, PHYBench, HLE and others) were reached by shortcuts such as numerical search or answer-first verification; direct evidence that final-answer scoring overstates scientific reasoning (preprint marked work in progress).

title: PhysElite: How Far Are LLMs from Solving Olympiad-Level Physics Problems?
notes: physics_science: should-cite - the newest large physics benchmark (11,586 olympiad problems with diagrams and bilingual step-by-step derivations; best model 33.7%), which adds a process-level evaluation of where reasoning chains fail; static items.

title: PhysicsArena: The First Multimodal Physics Reasoning Benchmark Exploring Variable, Process, and Solution Dimensions
notes: physics_science: should-cite - scores variable identification and physical-process formulation as well as the final solution on multimodal high-school physics problems; an intermediate-step evaluation in physics the revised paragraph should acknowledge.

title: Probing the Critical Point (CritPt) of AI Reasoning: a Frontier Physics Research Benchmark
notes: physics_science: should-cite - 71 unpublished research-level challenges written by 50+ physicists, decomposed into 190 checkpoints with machine-verifiable answers; the clearest instance of the research-physics strand the May sentence calls theoretical, and one of the benchmarks Ansari et al. audit.

title: Theoretical Physics Benchmark (TPBench) -- a Dataset and Study of AI Reasoning Capabilities in Theoretical Physics
authors: Daniel J. H. Chung et al.
notes: physics_science: should-cite - 57 novel high-energy-theory and cosmology problems from undergraduate to research level, graded by auto-verification and holistic grading; it supports the 'theoretical physics' characterisation, but only for this research-level strand.

title: PHYSICS: Benchmarking Foundation Models on University-Level Physics Problem Solving
notes: physics_science: should-cite - 1,297 expert-annotated university-level problems in six areas with automated answer evaluation (o3-mini 59.9%); a standard ACL-venue physics benchmark to list beside UGPhysics.

notes: physics_science: should-cite - physics, chemistry and biology olympiads from 2023-2026 (IPhO, IChO, USAPhO and others) graded by an LLM judge with process-credit rubrics calibrated against medallist ground truth; recency as contamination control and a judge-validity comparison point for EngTrace's residual judge.

title: FrontierScience: Evaluating AI's Ability to Perform Expert-Level Scientific Tasks
notes: physics_science: should-cite - expert-written physics, chemistry and biology problems in an olympiad track (short answers) and a research track graded with granular rubrics over the solution process (160 released as a gold set); the frontier-lab reference for expert-level science evaluation.

title: Humanity's Last Exam
notes: physics_science: should-cite - 2,500 expert-written, model-filtered closed-ended questions across dozens of subjects, graded on final answers; the frontier general suite the generalist-benchmark sentence now needs (published in Nature as 'A benchmark of expert-level academic questions to assess AI capabilities').

title: GPQA: A Graduate-Level Google-Proof Q&A Benchmark
notes: physics_science: should-cite - 448 expert-written multiple-choice questions in physics, chemistry and biology (experts 65%, skilled non-experts with web access 34%); the canonical graduate-level science suite, absent from the May paper although SuperGPQA is cited.

title: MMLU-Pro: A More Robust and Challenging Multi-Task Language Understanding Benchmark
notes: physics_science: should-cite - 12K+ reasoning-focused ten-option questions over 14 domains including physics, chemistry and engineering, with prompt sensitivity cut from 4-5% to 2%; the reasoning-oriented successor of the MMLU the May paper cites as factual recall.

title: OlympiadBench: A Challenging Benchmark for Promoting AGI with Olympiad-Level Bilingual Multimodal Scientific Problems
notes: physics_science: should-cite - 8,476 olympiad and Gaokao mathematics and physics problems with expert step-by-step solutions but automatic final-answer scoring (GPT-4V 10.74% on physics); the standard olympiad-physics reference later benchmarks compare against.

authors: Daman Arora, Himanshu Gaurav Singh, Mausam

title: SciCode: A Research Coding Benchmark Curated by Scientists

notes: physics_science: should-cite - ChemBench: 2,788 question-answer pairs (1,039 manual, 1,749 semi-automatic) tagged by skill and difficulty and compared with human chemists; the reference chemistry benchmark for EngTrace's chemical-engineering branch (arXiv title: 'Are large language models superhuman chemists?').

notes: physics_science: should-cite - 1,340 college-level materials-science problems from textbooks (946 with reference solutions, 315 with images) scored by rule-based checks with a 5% tolerance plus an LLM judge for formulas; the nearest physical-science analogue of EngTrace's deterministic-check-then-judge design, and adjacent to its mechanical and civil branches.
